title: How much does a bridging loan cost?
h1: How much does a bridging loan cost? (search-result title; H1 not independently confirmed)
summary: Blog article / guide explaining the components that make up the total cost of a UK bridging loan. Thesis: the headline monthly interest rate is only one part of the cost; the full picture is interest + lender arrangement fee + broker fees + legal fees + valuation fees (+ possible exit fee). Concrete guidance revealed by the search tool: monthly interest starts around 0.44%, with a common average near 1% per month (roughly 12% a year), depending on loan-to-value, location and credit profile; lender arrangement fee usually 1% to 2% of the loan (i.e. £5,000 to £10,000 on a £500,000 loan), sometimes waived on large loans; broker fee of about £1,500 on application plus 0.5% at offer and 0.5% at completion, worked example totalling £6,500 on a £500,000 loan; exit fees often around 1% can apply on repayment; valuation fees are covered but the figure was cut off in the snippet. The page states it offers a general overview rather than specific products or lender comparisons.

faq.q: How much does a bridging loan cost?
faq.a: Interest from about 0.44% per month, average near 1% per month (~12% a year), plus a lender arrangement fee of usually 1% to 2%, broker fees (about £1,500 + 0.5% at offer + 0.5% at completion), legal fees, valuation fees and possibly an exit fee of around 1% [a][b].

faq.q: What is the lender arrangement fee on a bridging loan?
faq.a: Usually 1% to 2% of the loan (£5,000 to £10,000 on £500,000); large loans may sometimes have it waived [a][b].

faq.q: What does a bridging loan broker charge?
faq.a: About £1,500 on application, plus 0.5% on offer and 0.5% on completion; example of £6,500 on a £500,000 loan [a][b].
Exit fees, often around 1%, can apply on repayment [b].
